subject: economics
chapter_title: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition

concepts.title: Characteristics of Perfect Competition
concepts.definition: A market structure marked by numerous buyers and sellers, homogeneous products, unrestricted entry and exit, and complete information, making firms price-takers.
concepts.key_idea: Firms sell identical products at a uniform market-determined price.
question_patterns: what are the main features of perfect competition
describe the market structure where firms are price takers
why is a competitive firm unable to influence market price
explain free entry and exit in perfect competition

solution_steps.explain: Because each firm sells a tiny share of homogeneous goods, raising price drops demand to zero while lowering price is unnecessary.

concepts.title: Total Revenue of a Firm
concepts.definition: The total dollar or rupee proceeds obtained by a producer from selling a specific quantity of output at the existing price.
concepts.key_idea: Total revenue increases linearly with output when price remains fixed.
question_patterns: calculate the total revenue of the firm
find total revenue when price is ... and quantity is ...
what is total revenue schedule for given prices
how does total revenue change with output under perfect competition

solution_steps.action: multiply unit price by output quantity
solution_steps.explain: TR is the product of market price and units sold

concepts.title: Average Revenue and Marginal Revenue
concepts.definition: Average revenue represents earnings per unit of output, whereas marginal revenue measures the additional income gained from selling one extra unit.
concepts.key_idea: For a price-taking firm, average revenue and marginal revenue are both identical to market price.
question_patterns: determine average revenue and marginal revenue
show that average revenue equals market price
why is marginal revenue equal to price under perfect competition
compute AR and MR schedules

solution_steps.explain: AR is total revenue divided by quantity sold
In perfect competition, extra revenue per unit equals market price

concepts.title: Profit Determination
concepts.definition: The net economic gain of a firm calculated as total revenue minus total explicit and implicit costs.
concepts.key_idea: A firm maximises economic profit by widening the surplus of revenue over costs.
question_patterns: calculate profit at each level of output
determine the firm's profit from total revenue and total cost
find the output level where profit is maximum
what is the profit level when price is ... and costs are ...

solution_steps.explain: TR equals market price multiplied by quantity

solution_steps.action: subtract total cost from total revenue
solution_steps.explain: profit is TR minus TC

concepts.title: Conditions for Profit Maximisation
concepts.definition: The three necessary criteria for profit-maximising output: price equals marginal cost, marginal cost is non-decreasing, and price covers variable or average costs.
concepts.formula: p = MC, MC_slope >= 0, p >= AVC (short run) or p >= AC (long run)
concepts.key_idea: Profit peaks where price equals rising marginal cost provided price covers minimum average variable cost.
question_patterns: what three conditions must hold for profit maximisation
explain why p = MC at profit-maximising output
can output be optimal on the falling part of MC curve
why must price exceed average variable cost in the short run

solution_steps.explain: Check if market price equals short-run or long-run marginal cost.
Ensure marginal cost is non-decreasing at the target output level.
Check that market price is greater than or equal to AVC in the short run or AC in the long run.

concepts.title: Short-Run and Long-Run Supply Curves
concepts.definition: The supply curve of a firm is the upward-sloping segment of its marginal cost curve on or above the minimum average variable cost in the short run and minimum average cost in the long run.
concepts.formula: supply_quantity = q(MC = p) for p >= min(AVC)
concepts.key_idea: The marginal cost curve determines output decisions above the shut-down threshold.
question_patterns: derive the short run supply curve of a competitive firm
what is the long run supply curve of a firm
explain shut down point and break even point
where does the short run supply curve originate

solution_steps.explain: In the short run, shut-down occurs at the minimum point of AVC where SMC cuts AVC.
For prices above minimum AVC, output follows the rising segment of SMC; for lower prices, supply is zero.

concepts.title: Market Supply Curve Aggregation
concepts.definition: The horizontal summation of individual firm supply curves showing total quantity supplied by all sellers at each price level.
concepts.key_idea: Aggregate market supply is derived by adding up output supplied by each firm at a given price.
question_patterns: compute the market supply schedule from individual supply schedules
how is the market supply curve derived from firm supply curves
calculate aggregate market supply for given price levels
find market supply when there are multiple identical firms

solution_steps.action: add supplies of individual firms at given price
solution_steps.explain: Sum individual outputs supplied at the specified price level

concepts.title: Price Elasticity of Supply
concepts.definition: A quantitative measure of how responsive output supplied is to changes in the market price of the good.
concepts.key_idea: Price elasticity of supply compares percentage change in quantity supplied to percentage change in price.
question_patterns: calculate price elasticity of supply
find elasticity of supply given initial and final price and output
what is the price elasticity when price rises from ... to ... and quantity changes from ... to ...
compute e_s for a competitive seller

solution_steps.action: compute change in quantity and price
solution_steps.explain: Subtract initial quantity from final quantity and initial price from final price
Difference between final and initial price
Percentage change in quantity supplied
Percentage change in market price

solution_steps.action: divide quantity percentage by price percentage
solution_steps.explain: Ratio of percentage change in quantity to percentage change in price

concepts.title: Elasticity of Supply from Revenue Changes
concepts.definition: Calculating supply elasticity by first deriving supplied quantities from total revenue and price data at two different market prices.
concepts.formula: quantity_1 = revenue_1 / price_1, quantity_2 = revenue_2 / price_2, e_s = ((quantity_2 - quantity_1) * price_1) / ((price_2 - price_1) * quantity_1)
concepts.key_idea: Total revenue divided by unit price yields supply quantity, from which price elasticity is evaluated.
question_patterns: a firm earns revenue of ... at price ... and revenue ... at price ... find price elasticity of supply
calculate e_s from initial price, initial revenue, new price, and new revenue
find price elasticity when price and total revenues are known

solution_steps.explain: Initial quantity sold is initial revenue divided by initial price
Final quantity sold is final revenue divided by final price
Difference between final and initial output
Difference between final and initial price
e_s = (change_q / quantity_1) / (change_p / price_1)

concepts.title: Finding Target Supply Quantity using Elasticity
concepts.definition: Determining the new output supplied following a price change when initial quantity, initial price, new price, and supply elasticity are known.
concepts.formula: change_q = (price_elasticity * quantity_1 * (price_2 - price_1)) / price_1, quantity_2 = quantity_1 + change_q
concepts.key_idea: Supply elasticity helps predict new output given a price shift.
question_patterns: at price ... a firm supplies ... units; if price changes to ... and elasticity is ... what quantity will it supply
calculate new quantity supplied using price elasticity
find target output after a price increase given elasticity of supply

solution_steps.explain: Subtract initial price from new price
change_q = e_s * quantity_1 * (change_p / price_1)
Add output increment to initial quantity

concepts.title: Finding Initial and Final Output Levels from Quantity Increase
concepts.definition: Deducing initial and final production levels from a known absolute increase in quantity supplied, given price variation and supply elasticity.
concepts.formula: quantity_1 = (change_quantity * price_1) / (price_elasticity * (price_2 - price_1)), quantity_2 = quantity_1 + change_quantity
concepts.key_idea: The absolute increase in output divided by proportionate price change scaled by elasticity yields original output.
question_patterns: market price changes from ... to ... resulting in quantity supplied increasing by ... units; if e_s = ... find initial and final output
calculate initial output when quantity supplied increases by fixed units and elasticity is given
find starting and ending quantities from output increase and supply elasticity

solution_steps.explain: Difference between final price and initial price
initial_quantity = (change_quantity * price_1) / (price_elasticity * change_p)
Add output increase to initial quantity
